answer: Sybils splitting into many identities pay staking and re-verification costs per identity, while honest agents amortize one stake across epochs. Each agent must stake tokens at a registered vertex in the identity graph, and every epoch a random beacon selects validators who re-verify a sample of peers' signed work history. An echo of each verification is broadcast to peers, so fake identities lacking genuine history get flagged and slashed, making mass forgery economically unprofitable. In practice, Agent0182 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
